**Scope(s):** METHODOLOGICAL · **Row count:** 8 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** CONTESTED · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** `Cycle 5 / Cycle 6 / Cycle 7`, `[CORPUS]/[REC]/[NEG]/[OPEN] tags`, `kernel candidates produced this cycle: zero` · **Aliases:** `Gita strand cyclical kernel-candidacy self-audit`, `external interpretive lens standing discipline`

Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.

## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)
- **OBJECT-INDEX** (batch B0065, scope METHODOLOGICAL): A recurring, numbered-cycle self-audit practice that re-tests, on each cycle's freshest corpus batch, whether the Bhagavad Gita reading strand should ever be promoted from an external interpretive lens to kernel-primitive status, explicitly run as a falsification attempt against the standing prior-cycle recommendation rather than as confirmation. Cycle 6 (this batch, S2702) maps kshetra/kshetrajna (13.1-2) onto the field/frame split and the 18.20-22 three-guna typology onto three already-measured Zero-projection failure modes, concluding six cycles have produced zero kernel primitives and three namings of pre-existing results, and states the one thing that would overturn the recommendation: a verse-derived claim yielding a testable prediction the theory does not already make. Cycle 7 (S2735) tests that exact criterion against KR-ZOOM-01's results: it finds the Gita's invariance-under-view intuition (2.16) is the first candidate of that shape in seven cycles -- and reports it CONTRADICTED by measurement (114 determination-loss cases across two splits, zero determination-gain cases), recording explicitly that 'a lens that only ever agrees is decorative' and that this is the first cycle in which the lens and the experiment disagree.
